name: LOCALREACH Form Monitor
author: LOCALREACH

sections.description:
LOCALREACH Form Monitor helps WordPress site owners and agencies check whether contact forms and WordPress mail handling are working as expected.

The WordPress.org version provides manual and scheduled checks, supported form monitoring, diagnostics, local test logs, customer reports and optional agency branding.

The plugin currently detects and supports checks around:

  • Contact Form 7
  • Elementor Pro forms
  • WPForms
  • Fluent Forms
  • WordPress wp_mail()

Typical use cases:

  • Run a quick manual mail test from the WordPress admin.
  • See which supported forms are present on a site.
  • Keep a local test log for troubleshooting and client documentation.
  • Check basic mail and configuration signals before handing over a website.
  • Schedule recurring monitoring and customer reports.
  • Customize customer-facing reports with optional agency branding.

The plugin does not replace professional mailbox monitoring, transactional email logging or deliverability auditing. It checks the WordPress side of the process and records whether WordPress and supported form integrations accepted the generated test request.

Included functionality

All functionality included in this WordPress.org package is available without a license key, payment, quota or trial period. This includes scheduled monitoring, customer reports and optional agency branding.

External services

LOCALREACH Form Monitor sends test and report emails through the WordPress mail system (wp_mail()) and supported local form plugin integrations. It does not connect to a LOCALREACH licensing service or add a separate third-party delivery service. If the site uses an SMTP, transactional email, DNS or security service, that service may process requests according to its own configuration.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin files to the /wp-content/plugins/localreach-form-monitor directory, or install the plugin through the WordPress plugins screen.
  2. Activate the plugin through the Plugins screen in WordPress.
  3. Open Form Monitor in the WordPress admin menu.
  4. Set a separate test mailbox for test messages.
  5. Run a manual mail test and review the diagnostics and test log.
sections.faq:
Which form plugins are supported?

The plugin currently detects and works with Contact Form 7, Elementor Pro forms, WPForms and Fluent Forms where the relevant plugin is active and the form can be identified.

Does the plugin guarantee inbox delivery?

No. The plugin checks whether WordPress and supported form integrations accept the generated test request and whether the configured mail handoff can be triggered. Inbox placement depends on the receiving mailbox, DNS, SMTP configuration, reputation and anti-spam systems.

Can the plugin send scheduled tests automatically?

Yes. Scheduled monitoring can be enabled in the plugin settings.

Are customer reports included in the free version?

Yes. Customer reports can be opened, emailed manually or scheduled from the plugin settings.

Does the plugin send real form submissions to customers?

The plugin is designed to use a separate test recipient for monitoring and testing. You should configure a dedicated test mailbox and avoid using real customer inboxes as the test recipient.

Can agencies use their own branding?

Yes. Agency branding is optional and can be configured in the report settings.

Does this plugin store personal data?

The plugin stores its own settings and test logs in the local WordPress database. Test logs can include technical test IDs, timestamps, test source, recipient address and status messages. Configure a dedicated test mailbox and avoid entering personal customer data into test fields unless it is necessary for your own process.
sections.changelog:
1.1.4

  • Replaced generic global prefixes and namespaces with product-specific identifiers.
  • Added automatic migration of settings, monitored forms, logs and scheduled events from earlier versions.
  • Isolated the bundled framework fallback under the Form Monitor namespace.

1.1.3

  • Added an explicit, disabled-by-default opt-in for LOCALREACH attribution in customer-facing reports.
  • Applied a final HTML allowlist after translating buffered admin, print and email output.
  • Kept all existing installations opted out unless an administrator actively enables attribution.

1.1.2

  • Made every function included in the WordPress.org package available without licensing or payment.
  • Removed the Freemius SDK and license controls from the WordPress.org package.
  • Replaced direct script and style output with WordPress enqueue APIs.
  • Removed default customer-facing attribution and corrected the contributor username.

1.1.1

  • Aligned the dashboard hero, action hierarchy, content width, color palette and cards with the CareReport UI.
  • Kept monitoring status colors and all existing feature and license behavior unchanged.

1.1.0

  • Integrated the LOCALREACH Plugin Framework dashboard and admin navigation.
  • Added a bundled framework fallback while preferring a compatible standalone framework.
  • Preserved all existing settings, logs, cron hooks and Free, Pro and Agency feature gates.

1.0.1

  • Tightened Free, Pro and Agency admin UI so plan-specific settings are only shown where they belong.
  • Moved customer report options into a dedicated Pro/Agency section.
  • Restricted white-label, agency contact data, report footer customization and internal agency notes to Agency.
  • Preserved hidden settings while saving lower-plan configurations.
  • Hardened report output so Agency branding is only rendered when the Agency feature gate allows it.

1.0.0

  • Initial stable release.
  • Added Freemius-based Free, Pro and Agency licensing.
  • Added safe fallback to Free when no active premium license is connected.
  • Added server-side feature gates for monitoring, scheduled tests, customer reports and white-label functions.
  • Added scheduled form monitoring with cron self-healing after license activation.
  • Added manual and monitored test support for Contact Form 7, Elementor Pro, WPForms and Fluent Forms.
  • Added customer report generation, report email delivery and printable reports.
  • Added diagnostics for WordPress mail handoff, monitored forms, scheduled tests and basic DNS signals.
